text: Let's make the difference from last lesson completely concrete — Delta tables versus Parquet tables.
The only code difference is one extra dot format delta call. Inspect the actual files inside either folder, and they look identical — Delta really is Parquet underneath, made completely literal here.

But describe history only works on the Delta table — it reads directly from the underscore delta underscore log from last lesson. The plain Parquet folder has nothing like this, because there's no log to describe the history of at all.

And here's the real-world payoff: two jobs writing to the same plain Parquet folder at once risk half-written, inconsistent files. The same two jobs writing to a Delta table get resolved cleanly by the transaction log — one write succeeds, or fails, never half.
One extra word on the write, one log underneath, and a real safety guarantee neither Parquet alone has. Next lesson: creating a Delta table, the real syntax, start to finish.
